merger_description:
SLR Australia Pty Ltd (**SLR**) proposes to acquire:

* 100% of the issued share capital in Spectrum Ecology Pty Ltd (**Spectrum**) from Cameron Mounsey;
* 94.34% of the issued share capital in Millcrest Technology Pty Ltd (**Millcrest**) from Cameron Mounsey as trustee for Mounsey Investment Trust; and
* 3.77% of the issued share capital in Millcrest from Christopher Parker and 1.89% of the issued share capital in Millcrest from Benjamin Boothby,

together, the **Acquisition**.

SLR is part of the SLR group of companies (**SLR Group**). In Australia, SLR Group supplies environmental consulting services to clients across the energy, finance, mining, infrastructure, manufacturing, and technology industries. Its services include strategic advisory, technical consulting and environmental, social, and governance advisory services, environmental risk assessments, impact assessments, engineering, scientific and technical services, ecological, efficient energy and water management services, and town planning and project management.

Spectrum is a specialist environmental consultancy providing terrestrial ecological consulting services primarily to the mining, infrastructure, energy and government sectors. Its services include flora and vegetation surveys, fauna surveys, spatial ecology and geographic information system (**GIS**) analysis, remote sensing, rehabilitation monitoring, environmental impact assessments, and environmental compliance reporting.

Millcrest supplies proprietary GIS and spatial analysis software, Tyton Ecological Intelligence (**Tyton**), which comprises TytonAI, an AI-powered vegetation classification software, and TytonIQ, a cloud-based environmental intelligence platform. Millcrest licenses the Tyton software to Spectrum and another independent consultancy based in Queensland.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is limited horizontal overlap between SLR and
Spectrum in the supply of environmental consulting
services, as SLR is a multidisciplinary environmental
consulting firm and Spectrum specialises in terrestrial
ecology consulting services
b. SLR’s and Spectrum’s combined shares of supply of
environmental consulting services and terrestrial
ecology consulting services nationally are estimated to
be low, the increment in shares of supply arising from
the Acquisition would be low, and there are alternative
providers in Australia
c. while there is a vertical relationship between the GIS
and spatial analysis software supplied by Millcrest and
the services supplied by SLR and Spectrum, there is low
risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical effects
arising from the Acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
